Association of the APOE ε4 allele with spontaneous supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage in a Chinese Han case–control sample
abstract: Objective The role of genes, especially APOE, in intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is significant. But ethnic differences on ICH remain unclear, especially in Chinese individuals. We explored the correlation between APOE and ICH in Chinese Han population.. Methods In this single-centre, retrospective, case-control study, we collected clinical data of supratentorial ICH patients and healthy people matched 1:1 with ICH from June 2023 to January 2025. We used the χ 2 test to explore differences in APOE genotypes and allele frequencies between the groups. We established different ICH prediction models with and without APOE data using Machine Learning and compared prediction efficiency by AUC, net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results We enrolled 237 ICH patients and 237 controls. There was a significant difference in ε4 allele distribution between two groups (P = 0.010,OR = 1.813,95% CI (1.149,2.860)); differences remained after stratification by deep ICH (P = 0.015, OR = 1.979, 95% CI (1.135,3.448)). The NRI and IDI between ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8139) and without (AUC = 0.8083) APOE genotypes were 0.3797(P<0.0001) and 0.0106(P = 0.0458). The NRI and IDI between ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8204) and without (AUC = 0.8150) the ε4 allele were 0.3556(P<0.0001) and 0.0090(P = 0.0734). The NRI and IDI between deep ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8182) and without (AUC = 0.8076) APOE genotypes were 0.3949(P = 0.0002) and 0.0202(P = 0.0145). The NRI and IDI between deep ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8304) and without (AUC = 0.8223) the ε4 allele were 0.4001(P = 0.0002) and 0.0116(P = 0.0635). Conclusions For Chinese Han population, APOE polymorphisms, especially the ε4 allele, may be risk factors for ICH and deep ICH.

title: Short-term outcomes and follow-up of NICU graduates in selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Background Neonatal health during the post-discharge period is critical, especially for infants discharged from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), who are at higher risk of complications and long-term developmental issues. In Sri Lanka, there are limited data on post-NICU follow-up, highlighting the need for research. This study aimed to evaluate the post-discharge follow-up status of neonates admitted to selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka. Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted between January 2025 and June 2025 in the NICUs of National Hospital Galle (NHG) and German-Sri Lanka Friendship Hospital for Women (GSLFHW). Neonates admitted within 28 days of birth who were discharged home or transferred to other wards were included; those who died before discharge or were transferred to another NICU or another hospital were excluded. A purposive sampling method was used. Follow-up assessments were conducted one week and one month after discharge. Data were collected using a structured guide on feeding status, feeding issues, medical problems, pharmacological management, follow-up visits, and developmental milestones. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, and descriptive statistics were presented as numbers and percentages. Results Respiratory distress was the most common reason for NICU admission (74.4%, n = 96). At discharge, 97.7% were breastfed, and most achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones: cognitive (92.2%, n = 119), motor (96.1%, n = 124), psychosocial (95.3%, n = 123), and communication (93.0%, n = 120). One week post-discharge, 94.4% were breastfed; feeding issues included poor sucking (12.7%, n = 16) and vomiting (6.3%, n = 8). Most infants met developmental milestones. One month post-discharge, 81.8% were breastfed, 10.9% were readmitted for complications, including infections, and the mean weight increased to 3.26 kg. Nearly all (99.1%) achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones by one month. Conclusion Most neonates showed favorable early post‑discharge status at one week and one month, with high rates of breastfeeding and attainment of age‑expected developmental milestones at these time points. While breastfeeding remained predominant, some experienced feeding difficulties and a small proportion required readmission or died. These findings describe very early outcomes only; continued and longer‑term follow‑up is essential to manage complications and support health outcomes beyond the first month. title: Liver abscess caused by Parvimonas micra originating from a fish bone: A case report
abstract: BACKGROUND Liver abscess is an infectious lesion commonly caused by bacteria, Entamoeba histolytica , or fungi. Although Parvimonas micra (P. micra ) predominantly colonizes the orodigestive tract, liver abscesses associated with this bacterium are rarely reported. CASE SUMMARY A 52-year-old Chinese male patient presented to our emergency department with intermittent fever, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distention for 12 days. These symptoms showed no significant improvement following treatment at the primary care hospital. Initial liver ultrasound revealed a 7 cm infectious left lobe lesion. Anaerobic blood cultures and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry performed on admission and 2 days later both identified P. micra , suggesting that the liver abscess may have been caused by a foreign body originating from the digestive tract. Targeted examinations were performed. Abdomen enhanced computed tomography revealed a strip-shaped foreign body in the left outer lobe of the liver, extending to the wall of the pyloric canal. Simultaneous upper endoscopy and endoscopic ultrasonography detected a red scar in the gastric corpus and a 23.5 mm strip-shaped lesion within the liver mass, with one end penetrating the liver. The patient underwent laparoscopic left lateral liver lobectomy of the abscess and gastric perforation repair, during which a 3 cm fish bone was removed. He recovered fully after a targeted antibiotic regimen of penicillin G followed by piperacillin-tazobactam. This case is the first report of a liver abscess caused by P. micra due to ingestion of foreign bodies. CONCLUSION The clinical course of this patient highlights that the identification of P. micra and the detection of a foreign body within the liver mass provided pivotal clues for timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

title: The User Experience of Hyperloop: (User Survey, User Journey, User Experience, Station Operations and Boarding)
abstract: The advancement of transportation technologies has intensified the search for systems that meet rising mobility demands while reducing travel time and environmental impact. Hyperloop, a high-speed transport concept combining the speed of air travel with rail efficiency, has been studied technically, but passenger experience remains underexplored. This study addresses that gap through a User Journey framework integrating survey data and design expertise. Stakeholder in-sights were gathered through 56-questions and a comprehensive User Journey framework was developed by analysing touchpoints from conventional train and aircraft travel. Seven journey stages were identified: journey planning, travel to station, station experience, platform waiting, onboard experience, arrival/interchange, and onward travel. Key operational principles are mentioned by the respondents including self-service and flexible booking for planning; multi-modal integration and dynamic pricing for travel to station; 15–30-min station wait times with sub-10-min boarding; onboard vehicle capacities of 10–80 passengers with optimized seating and carry-on luggage; and efficient disembarking with seamless multimodal connections and service support on arrival. Overall survey findings highlight passenger preferences for a service model that integrates the convenience, accessibility, and comfort of high-speed rail with the speed of air travel. This research was conducted under Task 2.2 of the EU project Hyper4Rail.

Comorbid conditions account for nearly one-third of unacceptable disability cases after lumbar decompressive surgery.
abstract: Purpose To determine the proportion of patients with unacceptable disability secondary to comorbid (non-lumbar) conditions following lumbar decompressive surgery. Methods This single-centre study analysed prospectively collected data from 1,524 who underwent surgery between 01/01/2020 and 30/06/2025. We used postoperative Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) scores to classify patients as having acceptable disability (ODI ≤ 22) or unacceptable disability (ODI > 22). Patients with ODI > 22 were categorised by disability primarily attributable to either a lumbar or comorbid condition, based on clinical assessment and medical record review. We compared baseline characteristics and outcomes across disability groups. Results Twelve-month ODI was completed by 78.3% (1,193/1,524), while 14.2% (216/1,524) completed their last ODI at three months. Comorbid conditions accounted for 29.2% (150/514) of unacceptable disability at 12 months and 30.1% (31/103) of last ODI at three months. Forty-four of 150 (29.3%) with a 12-month comorbid condition achieved acceptable disability at three months before worsening. The most frequent comorbid conditions were lower-limb joint osteoarthritis, multiple conditions, brain diseases, cervicogenic disorders, and lower-limb musculoskeletal disorders. Notable baseline factors associated with comorbid condition included older age, female sex, previous lower-limb arthroplasty, public-funded healthcare, current smoker, ASA class 3, and anxiety/depression. Comorbid condition was associated with prolonged length of stay ( p = 0.042). Conclusion Comorbid conditions account for more than 29% of cases with unacceptable disability after lumbar decompressive surgery. Extended postoperative access to specialist review is needed to ensure accurate diagnosis and treatment. National spinal registries should capture postoperative events and comorbid conditions that affect patient-reported outcomes to support accurate clinical interpretation.

title: Psychological Readiness for the Green Energy Transition: A Human-Factors Model for Aviation Maintenance Crews
journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
abstract: Green-aviation research on battery and alternative-fuel chemistries has advanced rapidly, but a persistent blind spot remains: the psychological readiness of the maintenance personnel who operate these systems daily under safety-critical conditions.Silver-zinc (Ag-Zn) batteries, used in fighter aircraft for their high energy density, evolve hydrogen and oxygen gas through electrolysis of their alkaline electrolyte during charging -a hazard that builds invisibly over 36-to-72-hour charge cycles and becomes dangerous only once hydrogen concentration crosses its lower explosion limit.Managing this hazard depends less on chemistry knowledge and more on sustained technician vigilance during a long, low-stimulation monitoring task -precisely the condition under which classic vigilancedecrement research shows attentional lapses emerge, independent of training or competence.Drawing on the author's two decades as an aviation electrical maintenance engineer and a second career in applied and clinical psychology within the same defence environment, this paper argues that emerging green-energy-storage chemistries (lithium-ion, solidstate, hydrogen fuel cells) will introduce comparable low-visibility, highconsequence hazards, and that maintenance-crew psychological readiness must be engineered alongside the chemistry itself.Integrating self-efficacy theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, and vigilance-decrement research, the paper proposes a Psychology-Chemistry Interface Model with three components -chemistry-literacy calibration, hazardtolerability screening, and stress-buffered reporting culture -and a training framework for building calibrated, sustained vigilance in ground crews adopting new energy chemistries, including a low-cost toolkit -a pre-task hazard card, a vigilance-rotation roster, a hazard-tolerability selfcheck, and an added prompt within existing incident-reporting procedures -deployable at a single maintenance unit without new infrastructure.

title: A Modular Architecture for a Shunting-as-a-Service Simulation Tool in Rail Freight Terminals
abstract: The competitiveness of rail freight depends largely on the efficiency of shunting operations, which remain labour-intensive, time-consuming, and poorly digitalized. The Horizon Europe project AutoMoTIF addresses this challenge by developing and testing an Open Digital Twin Reference Architecture (ODTRA) to enable scalable and interoperable automation in multimodal terminals. This paper focuses on Use Case 3 (UC3), which investigates the concept of Shunting-as-a-Service (SaaS) through a modular simulation architecture applied to an intermodal terminal in Northern Italy. Two scenarios are analysed: the current layout, constrained by existing infrastructure, and a future terminal redesign enabling leaner operations. Both scenarios integrate key enablers such as fully autonomous multimodal locomotives, Digital Automatic Coupling (DAC), and automated gates. The proposed architecture will allow simulation of workflows, generation of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and assessment of safety, efficiency, and interoperability benefits. By framing shunting as a customizable digital service, the SaaS concept is expected to extend beyond technical automation towards a service-oriented business model, aiming at a scalable deployment of automation modules across inland freight terminals. The architecture presented in this work will serve as a basis for the development of a modular solution that could be applied to other rail freight terminals.
